This was done primarily for religious/ritualistic reasons (as it was forbidden to bury a pregnant woman) and later to save the child's life. The Name Change: The law was later referred to as the Lex Caesarea (Imperial Law) during the era of the Roman Emperors (Caesars). Caesar's Birth is a Myth: The popular belief that Julius Caesar himself was born via this procedure (and therefore is called a Caesarean section) is a myth. His mother, Aurelia, lived for many years after his birth, and until the modern era, the procedure on a living woman was almost invariably fatal.
